`import "./user"` and `import "./user.js"` can name the same file. Browsers and Node.js only accept the second in ES modules, while bundlers and Bun accept both. This rule keeps a project on one style, for all files or per extension.

It checks `import`, `export ... from`, `import()` and `require()`. Built-in modules and bare package names such as `"react"` or `"@babel/core"` are never checked.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* file "user.js" */}
```js
export function createUser(name) {
  return { name };
}
```

{/* bad {"options": ["always"]} */}
```js
import { createUser } from "./user";
```

Not reported:

{/* file "user.js" */}
```js
export function createUser(name) {
  return { name };
}
```

{/* good {"options": ["always"]} */}
```js
import { createUser } from "./user.js";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { useState } from "react";
```

## Options

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"import/extensions" = ["error", "never", { json = "always" }]
```

The first option sets the style for every extension:

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `"never"` (default) | Report an extension that the path does not need: `./user.js` where `./user` finds the same file. |
| `"always"` | Report a path without an extension. |
| `"ignorePackages"` | Like `"always"`, but paths into packages such as `"lodash/fp/map"` are not checked. |

{/* file "user.js" */}
```js
export function createUser(name) {
  return { name };
}
```

{/* bad {"options": ["never"]} */}
```js
import { createUser } from "./user.js";
```

{/* bad {"options": ["always"]} */}
```js
import map from "lodash/fp/map";
```

{/* good {"options": ["ignorePackages"]} */}
```js
import map from "lodash/fp/map";
```

An object after it, or in its place, has exceptions and more settings:

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| an extension, such as `js` or `json` | the first option | `"always"` or `"never"` for files with that extension. |
| `pattern` | `{}` | The same extension entries, in their own object. Use it if you also set one of the options below, because entries written next to those are ignored. |
| `ignorePackages` | `false` | Do not require an extension in paths into packages. |
| `checkTypeImports` | `false` | Also require extensions in `import type` and `export type`. |
| `pathGroupOverrides` | `[]` | A list of `{ pattern, action }`. A path that matches the glob `pattern` is skipped if `action` is `"ignore"`. With `"enforce"` it is checked even if it looks like a package. Only read if `pattern`, `ignorePackages` or `checkTypeImports` is set too. |

{/* good {"options": ["never", {"json": "always"}]} */}
```js
import { createUser } from "./user";
import settings from "./settings.json";
```

{/* good {"options": ["always"]} */}
```ts
import type { User } from "./user";
```

{/* bad {"options": ["always", {"checkTypeImports": true}]} */}
```ts
import type { User } from "./user";
```

{/* bad {"options": ["ignorePackages"]} */}
```js
import { routes } from "~/generated/routes";
```

{/* good {"options": ["always", {"ignorePackages": true, "pathGroupOverrides": [{"pattern": "~/generated/**", "action": "ignore"}]}]} */}
```js
import { routes } from "~/generated/routes";
```

To learn which file `./user` stands for, the rule tries `.mjs`, `.js`, `.json` and `.node`, like Node.js. It does not find `./user.ts`. So a `ts` entry has no effect, and `"never"` does not report `./user.ts`:

{/* file "user.ts" */}
```ts
export function createUser(name: string) {
  return { name };
}
```

{/* good {"options": ["never"]} */}
```ts
import { createUser } from "./user.ts";
```

In an ESLint config, `settings["import/resolver"]` changes how files are found.
